# Frontend Design-Token Modernization

Systematically modernize a legacy server-rendered frontend into a coherent,
accessible, themeable design system — without breaking the backend or shipping
visibly broken pages.

**Core principle:** A design system is a *contract*, not a paint job. The work
is (1) define tokens, (2) audit the templates for class drift, (3) rewrite
templates + CSS + JS together so every reference resolves, (4) verify
mechanically before declaring done. Skipping the contract step produces a
prettier version of the same inconsistency.

## When to Use

Trigger when the user asks to modernize, redesign, or "fix the look" of a
server-rendered app that shows most of these signals:

- Generic dark theme with no brand, no scale, no type hierarchy
- Mixed class systems (`.btn` *and* `.btn-custom` *and* inline styles)
- Templates reference classes that don't exist in the CSS (dead refs)
- Emoji in headings/buttons (🔒, ⚠️, 🔶) instead of icon system
- No focus rings, no skip-link, no reduced-motion handling
- Severity/status badges with different shapes per page
- Tables, alerts, and cards each have their own inconsistent styling
- Two parallel styling systems (e.g. a self-contained printable report
  vs the main app — leave the standalone report alone)

Do NOT use for:
- Greenfield projects (build with tokens from day 1; this skill is migration)
- Pure SPAs / React / Next.js (use nextjs-* skills instead)
- One-off design mockups (use claude-design or sketch)

## Step 0 — Scope and reconnaissance

Before any code change, map the surface:

1. List the templates directory and count files.
2. Read `app.py` / routes to know which template renders for which URL.
3. For each template, extract: blocks used, base layout, asset paths.
4. Identify self-contained templates (e.g. generated report HTML, print
   views, email templates). These keep their own styles; do not fold
   them into the design system.
5. Look for class-name drift between templates and CSS — common symptom
   is `class="badge-red"` in a template and `badge-red` missing in CSS
   (or only `badge-custom badge-red` defined). Use `search_files` to
   collect the union of used-vs-defined classes.

If the user supplied a `ui-ux-pro-max`-style skill and it loaded, prefer it
for color/type aesthetic guidance. If not, the design-token recipe in
`references/design-token-recipe.md` is the default.

## Step 1 — Define the design tokens

Pick a color space, font stack, and scale once, then enforce everywhere.

**Color space:** OKLCH (perceptually uniform; what Linear/Vercel/shadcn use).
Define tokens for `--bg-{1..4}`, `--surface`, `--border`, `--text`,
`--text-mute`, `--text-dim`, and a semantic set:
`--green --amber --red --blue --cyan --purple` each at `oklch(L C h / α)`.

**Type:** Two faces max. Body in Inter (or system fallback), code in
JetBrains Mono. Define `--fs-{xs,sm,md,lg,xl,2xl,3xl}` and `--lh-{tight,base,loose}`.

**Spacing:** 4px base. `--space-{1..8}` = 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64.

**Radius:** `--radius-{sm,md,lg,full}` = 4, 8, 12, 9999.

**Shadow:** `--shadow-{sm,md,lg}` — multi-layer for depth.

**Motion:** `--ease-{out,in-out}`, `--dur-{fast,base,slow}`. Pair with
`@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block that flattens all motion.

**Theme strategy:** Two schemes (light + dark) via `[data-theme="…"]` on
`<html>`. Store preference in `localStorage` (`scanner-theme` style key),
default to OS preference (`prefers-color-scheme`). Listen for OS changes
ONLY when user hasn't set a manual override.

Write tokens once at `:root`, override them in `[data-theme="light"]`.

## Step 2 — Class taxonomy

Group utilities so the same name does the same thing everywhere:

| Category   | Examples                                                 |
| ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| Buttons    | `.btn`, `.btn-primary`, `.btn-ghost`, `.btn-danger`, `.btn-sm`, `.btn-icon` |
| Badges     | `.badge-custom`, `.badge-{green,amber,red,blue,dim,critical,high,medium,low,info}` |
| Alerts     | `.alert-custom`, `.alert-{red,green,amber,blue}`         |
| Cards      | `.card`, `.card-header`, `.card-body`, `.stat-card`     |
| Tables     | `.table-custom`, `.table-compact`                        |
| Forms      | `.form-input`, `.form-select`, `.form-label`, `.form-help`, `.form-error` |
| Layout     | `.container`, `.grid`, `.stack`, `.cluster`, `.sidebar`  |
| Utilities  | `.font-mono`, `.text-{mute,dim,cyan}`, `.cell-truncate`, `.empty-state` |
| States     | `.spin-slow`, `.alert-link`, `.status-dot`              |

**Critical:** every class name used in any template MUST exist in CSS, and
every class defined in CSS should be used somewhere. The first rule is
non-negotiable; the second is a soft sweep at the end.

## Step 3 — Template rewrite order

Do the base layout LAST so child templates are designed against the new
classes, then extend base once. Order:

1. Static asset (style.css) — token system + class taxonomy
2. JS layer (app.js) — theme toggle, modals, filter chips, search
3. **Leaf templates first** (no children): scan_form, remote_scan_form,
   ai_config, mcp_panel, coverage, manifest, report, tree, finding_card
4. **Composite templates**: dashboard, results, findings
5. **Base layout last** (base.html): semantic structure, sidebar, skip-link,
   theme toggle button, block content hooks

This order means you never re-touch a child after base changes, and the
base layout can wire in any feature the children need.

### Semantic HTML discipline

- Replace `<div class="row">` with proper `<header>`, `<nav>`, `<main>`, `<aside>`, `<footer>`.
- Every interactive non-`<a>/<button>` element gets `role` + `tabindex` or is
  converted to a real button.
- Add `aria-label` to icon-only buttons.
- Add a "Skip to content" link as the first focusable element.
- Use `<i class="bi bi-…">` (Bootstrap Icons) for ALL icons. Replace emoji
  headings and emoji badges with icons — emoji don't honor theme, don't
  have accessible labels, and break monospace alignment.

### Inline style zero-tolerance

Search every template for `style="` and replace with the appropriate class.
Exceptions: dynamic values you can't pre-define (computed progress widths,
`--fs-xs` typography in tight tables, percentages on stat cards). Even
those should use CSS variables when possible: `style="width: {{ pct }}%"`.

## Step 4 — JS layer changes

The legacy app.js in this class usually has:
- Hard-coded HTML strings for status/severity badges (`STATUS_HTML` map)
- Inline `style.cssText` on dynamically-created elements
- Emoji characters in JS-rendered HTML
- No theme toggle handler

Rewrite to:
- Use `data-` attribute selectors (`data-theme-toggle`, `data-modal-open`,
  `data-modal-close`, `data-filter-group`, `data-search-filter`) so JS
  binds to semantics, not class names.
- Provide helpers `showFlash`, `openModal`, `closeModalById`, `copyText`
  and expose via `window.App`.
- Provide a `sevBadgeHtml(level)` / `statusBadgeHtml(status)` helper that
  returns the same HTML used in templates — one source of truth.
- Read theme from `localStorage`, write via `setTheme(theme)`, listen for
  `prefers-color-scheme` change but only when no manual override.
- Use `navigator.clipboard.writeText` with a textarea fallback for
  non-HTTPS contexts (see `browser-graceful-degradation` skill).

## Step 5 — Verification (do not skip — and "do not skip" means
        "against the bytes the running server returns, not the bytes
        you wrote")

This is the step most often faked. The agent rewrites templates, then
declares done because the files on disk look right. But the running
Flask process may be a different process from the one you started —
owned by the user, started before the session, with `debug=False` and
`use_reloader=False`, so Jinja templates and any module-level state
are frozen at server-startup time. CSS and JS are usually reloaded
per request; **templates, Python routes, and the Jinja loader are
not**. Treat them as immutable until the server restarts.

Run these BEFORE declaring done, in this order:

1. **Own the running server.** `lsof -nP -iTCP:<port> -sTCP:LISTEN`
   and inspect every Python process. If a PID you don't own is on
   the port, decide explicitly: kill-and-restart (acceptable for an
   ephemeral dev server, but tell the user) OR stop claiming that
   your edits have taken effect. There is no third option — "the
   templates are updated on disk" is not verification when the
   running process isn't reading from disk.
2. **Python parses:** `python3 -c "import ast; ast.parse(open('app.py').read())"`
3. **JS parses:** `node -c static/app.js`
4. **All Jinja templates parse:** loop with `jinja2.Environment().parse()`
5. **Class consistency:** collect every `class="…"` token from templates
   and compare against CSS rule selectors. Any template class missing
   from CSS is a runtime visual bug. Run this BEFORE the boot test so
   you fix gaps in the CSS, not in templates.
6. **Boot the server YOURSELF** (kill any user-owned process first):
   `python3 app.py` in background, then `curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:N/`
   for a 200, and `curl` each route listed in `app.url_map`. Any 500
   = template error. Read the actual 500 body — Werkzeug prints the
   failing template line and the BuildError for bad url_for calls;
   do not assume "server is up" means everything renders.
7. **Smoke-test theme toggle:** `curl` the rendered HTML and check
   `[data-theme-toggle]` is present. Empty = wiring is broken even
   though the server returns 200.
8. **Cross-check the bytes you wrote against the bytes the server
   sent.** `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:N/ | grep '<class signature
   from your new template>'` — if your edit doesn't appear in the
   response, the running process is NOT serving your files. This
   is the single check that catches the "verified by looking at
   disk" failure mode. Make it the LAST thing you do before the
   browser navigation step.
9. **Live-browser visual confirmation:** drive `browser_navigate`
   to each rendered URL, take a screenshot, then re-read it with
   `vision_analyze`. Prefer literal yes/no questions (`"Is there a
   left sidebar? Yes or no."`) over open-ended descriptions — see
   Pitfall: vision hallucination below.
10. **Cross-check HTML ground truth:** the browser DOM snapshot is
    the ground truth, not the vision model's prose. If
    `browser_vision` says "no tables visible" but the snapshot lists
    `table > row > cell` nodes, trust the snapshot.

If iteration budget runs out before step 8, do steps 1–5 and report
honestly that the user should restart the server themselves — do not
invent a "looks good" verdict, do not claim "verification complete",
do not screenshot something you haven't first confirmed is the
served output of your edits.

## Pitfalls

- **Emoji badges can't be themed or read by screen readers.** Replace.
- **Mixed class systems** (`.btn` and `.btn-custom` both present) means
  templates drifted over time. Pick one naming scheme and rewrite — don't
  add aliases. Aliases become permanent debt.
- **`sev_color` / `sev_label` undefined in app.py** — common bug. Don't
  introduce it; resolve severity to a badge class inline in the template.
- **Self-contained templates** (print reports, generated HTML, emails)
  intentionally have their own embedded styles. Leave them alone unless
  the user asks for a unified system.
- **Theme flash on load** (FOUC). The toggle must set `data-theme` on
  `<html>` BEFORE first paint — either inline a small script in `<head>`
  that reads localStorage, or accept the flash and move on.
- **Server-rendered dashboards with setTimeout poll loops** — keep the
  poll cadence but bind to the same `data-` selectors you standardized.
- **Reduced motion** — `:focus-visible` ring animation should be
  unconditionally enabled (accessibility > aesthetics); only motion on
  large surfaces (page transitions, skeleton shimmer) should respect
  `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- **Inline `style="background: var(--red)"` for status colors** works
  but defeats the design system. Extract a `.progress-fill.is-failed`
  class and write `class="progress-fill is-failed"` instead.
- **Empty `<i>` icon tags** when Bootstrap Icons CSS hasn't loaded —
  verify Bootstrap Icons `<link>` is in base.html before relying on
  `bi-*` classes.
- **JS selector binding drift** — JS uses `[data-theme-toggle]` but the
  template only wrote `id="theme-toggle"` (no `data-` attribute). The
  button silently does nothing. Pick the selector name once and use it
  in BOTH files; if you standardize on `data-*` for delegation, add
  `data-theme-toggle` alongside `id=` rather than relying on one or the
  other. Quickest check after the rewrite: `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:N/ |
  grep 'data-theme-toggle'` — empty = the wiring is broken.
- **Server was started before the session** — if `lsof -iTCP:5050`
  shows a Python process running but it's not the one you started, the
  user owns it and template edits won't take effect until they restart.
  The temptation here is to keep working as if the edits took effect —
  "the templates are updated on disk" is not verification. The test is
  trivial: `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:N/ | grep -F '<unique string from
  your new template>'`. If the grep is empty, the server is serving the
  OLD template. Kill and restart, or stop claiming completion. There is
  no soft middle. CSS/JS are usually reloaded per request and will
  update live; templates, routes, and Jinja filters are not.
- **Vision model hallucination on screenshots** — `browser_vision`
  (the auxiliary vision fallback) often returns generic, confident,
  wrong descriptions ("The image shows a Security Audit Report dashboard"
  when the page is a settings form). `vision_analyze` with a literal
  yes/no question and the local screenshot path produces more reliable
  answers, but still verify against the browser DOM snapshot. Never
  accept the vision model's prose as evidence — it is decoration.
- **Inherited CSS variables on dynamically-inserted elements** — when
  you write `style.cssText` in JS, you may overwrite inherited tokens.
  Use `className` instead, or append `;color: var(--text)` rather than
  replacing the whole cssText.

## Verification script

```bash
bash scripts/verify-modernization.sh <project-root>
```

Runs Python AST parse, JS parse, Jinja2 parse of every template, and a
class-vs-CSS consistency check. Exits non-zero on any failure.

## Support files

- `scripts/verify-modernization.sh` — deterministic 5-step pre-flight
- `references/design-token-recipe.md` — full token values (light + dark OKLCH),
  class taxonomy cheatsheet, Bootstrap Icons reference list
- `references/worked-example-security-scanner-v14.md` — concrete run on a
  14-template Flask+Jinja scanner app: scope carve-out for build-artifact
  templates, severity helper pattern, full verification ladder that
  caught a real JS selector binding bug. **Now includes a
  session-2 follow-up documenting the "verified by looking at disk"
  failure mode** (server owned by user → template edits invisible
  until restart), the missing-endpoint 500 pattern (url_for
  references that don't exist in app.url_map), the `s.id` vs
  `s.get('scan_id')` registry-key gotcha, and a pre-flight script
  to catch all three before declaring done.

## Session-2 follow-up: the "verification is complete" failure

The previous run on this project shipped looking-good-ish, and the
user said "the design still messed up". The actual root causes were
not what was reported at the time:

1. **The Flask process was the user's, started before the session.**
   The first run "verified" by looking at the rewritten files on
   disk, never by curling the served HTML. The browser had been
   rendering the legacy templates the whole time. Test:
   `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:5050/ | grep -F '<unique string from
   your new template>'` — empty grep means the server is serving the
   OLD template.
2. **The new templates referenced url_for endpoints that did not
   exist:** `index` (real: `dashboard`), `new_scan` (`scan_form`),
   `new_remote_scan` (`remote_scan_form`), `scan_results`
   (`view_results`), `scan_status` (no endpoint), `coverage` at top
   level (no endpoint), `download_artifact` (no endpoint). Each one
   caused a Werkzeug `BuildError` 500. The fix is to grep
   `url_for\(['\"]([^'\"]+)` across every template, then verify
   each named endpoint exists in the app's `app.url_map` BEFORE
   booting the server.
3. **The scan-registry dict uses key `"id"`, not `"scan_id"`.**
   So `s.get('scan_id')` returned None, url_for raised
   BuildError(missing value), and every dashboard row 500'd.
   Template fix: use `s.id` or `s['id']`.
4. **`download_artifact` did not exist** as a route. Added a new
   route `/results/<scan_id>/artifact/<path:filename>` with
   path-traversal protection (`..` segment check + realpath
   containment under scan_dir + `isfile` check).

Fixes applied this session:
- `templates/base.html`: `index`→`dashboard`, `new_scan`→`scan_form`,
  `new_remote_scan`→`remote_scan_form`, removed top-level Coverage
  nav (no endpoint).
- Bulk-patched `scan_results`→`view_results` and `s.get('scan_id')`→
  `s.id` / `scan.id`→`scan['id']` across all 14 templates.
- Replaced remaining `scan_status` refs with `view_results`.
- Added `download_artifact` route to `app.py`.

What was still pending at the end of the session: actual verification
that the third restart returned HTTP 200 with the new design rendered.
The 54 missing CSS classes (`.stat-card`, `.artifact-list`,
`.evidence-box`, `.poc-box`, `.drop-zone`, `.step-list`, `.form-row`,
`.btn-sm`, `.flex-between`, `.grid-2-1`, `.col-stack`, `.meta`,
`.label`, `.severity-badge`, `.flag`, `.verified`, `.finding-detail`,
`.finding-row`, etc.) were not added to `style.css` in this session
and will render unstyled until they are.

## Pre-flight check for next session on this project

```bash
# 1. Confirm the server is yours
lsof -nP -iTCP:5050 -sTCP:LISTEN

# 2. Confirm templates are being served (sampling unique markers)
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:5050/ | grep -q 'app-sidebar' || echo "OLD TEMPLATES"

# 3. Confirm endpoints exist for every url_for reference
python3 -c "
import re, glob
endpoints = set()
with open('app.py') as f: app = f.read()
for m in re.finditer(r'@app\.route\([^)]+\)\s*\n\s*def\s+(\w+)', app):
    endpoints.add(m.group(1))
for path in glob.glob('templates/*.html'):
    with open(path) as f: text = f.read()
    for m in re.finditer(r\"url_for\(['\\\"]([^'\\\"]+)['\\\"]\", text):
        ep = m.group(1)
        if ep not in endpoints:
            print(f'  MISSING endpoint: {ep}  (referenced in {path})')
"

# 4. Confirm CSS has every class templates use
python3 -c "
import re, glob
css = open('static/style.css').read()
for path in glob.glob('templates/*.html'):
    with open(path) as f: text = f.read()
    for m in re.finditer(r'class=\"([^\"]+)\"', text):
        for cls in m.group(1).split():
            if cls and not re.search(r'\.' + re.escape(cls) + r'\b', css):
                print(f'  MISSING CSS: .{cls}  (used in {path})')
" | head -20
```

If any of these print, fix them BEFORE declaring the redesign done.
